title: Cross-Architecture Feature Universality: Do Emotion-Representing SAE Features Align Between GPT-2 and Llama-3.2-1B?

original_idea.problem: Whether the same abstract concepts are represented by geometrically similar features across different models is an open question.
original_idea.direction: Train SAEs on GPT-2-small and Llama-3.2-1B. Use automated interpretability to identify emotion-related features. Compute cosine similarity. Test steering.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: feature universality would allow interpretability findings to transfer across models, massively reducing the cost of understanding new models. Its absence would imply each model requires independent work. This directly impacts the feasibility of the scalable oversight agenda.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Training SAEs on two different architectures, implementing automated interpretability pipelines, computing cross-model feature similarity, and testing steering all require significant interpretability experience. The multi-step pipeline is challenging for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multiple stages: train 2 SAEs, run automated labeling, compute similarity, test steering. The full pipeline is long. A reduced version (just the similarity comparison without steering) would be more scoped but still requires SAE training and automated labeling.

novelty.reasoning: 'Quantifying Feature Space Universality Across Large Language Models via Sparse Autoencoders' (arXiv:2410.06981) directly studies cross-model SAE feature universality across GPT-2, Mistral-7B, and Llama-3 8B, finding correlated features and semantically similar arrangements (e.g., circular 'months' features). Emotion-related concepts specifically show higher cross-model similarity. 'Universal Sparse Autoencoders: Interpretable Cross-Model Concept Alignment' (arXiv:2502.03714) further develops cross-model alignment methods. The proposed GPT-2 vs Llama-3.2-1B emotion feature comparison is substantially addressed by these existing studies.
